$comment: D-FFI-DARWIN-MALLOC-ZONE-TAIL-OPAQUE — the gate-resident RUNTIME witness for the 22 members that shipped as one opaque 176-byte `__opaque_tail` until P48. WHY IT EXISTS, and why the unit pin is not enough: tests/ffi/test_darwin_struct_shapes.cpp asserts what the DESCRIPTOR says (names, order, offsets, the 200-byte total, typedef-equals-tag identity, and two REMOVE-direction mutants), but a self-consistent WRONG table passes a descriptor test perfectly. The other question — does the table agree with the real libmalloc — can only be asked at RUN time, and this example asks it: every offset is read through a `malloc_zone_t *` that `malloc_default_zone()` returned, i.e. a struct libsystem_malloc laid out and this program did not, so a slid offset yields a WRONG VALUE from live memory instead of a consistent lie. The version / zone_name / introspect guards are what convert 'the arithmetic is internally consistent' into 'the arithmetic agrees with Apple's'. THE 4-BYTE TAIL PAD is the subtle cell and is pinned twice: `unsigned version` is 4 bytes at 104 and the next member must 8-align, so `memalign` is at 112 and 108..111 is padding — guard 8 catches a `version` modelled 8 bytes wide or a dropped pad, and the exit sum restates it as (offMemalign - offVersion - 8) == 0. THE CALLABLE MEMBERS ARE INVOKED, not merely addressed: taking &z->malloc proves the OFFSET, calling it proves the SIGNATURE, and a wrong parameter list on a member Apple's allocator implements is precisely the silent-miscompile class the opaque tail existed to avoid — size, malloc, calloc, realloc, free and memalign are each driven through the live default zone and cross-checked against invariants (usable >= requested; realloc preserves the seeded bytes; calloc really zeroes; memalign really 64-aligns) or against the shipped free function malloc_size, never against a literal. HERMETIC: no size, address, page size, allocator version or zone name is compared to a literal — `version` need only lie in a sane open range, the name and introspection table need only be non-null, every block is freed back to its zone, `memalign` is gated on version >= 5 (the version Apple documents it from) so an older allocator skips rather than fails, and the default zone is never destroyed. NOT CALLED, deliberately: destroy, batch_malloc, batch_free, pressure_relief, claimed_address, try_free_default, malloc_with_options and the five malloc_type_* entries are typed by the descriptor but are optional-and-may-be-NULL by Apple's own comments, version-gated above the live allocator, or destructive; their offsets are still bounded because malloc_type_malloc_with_options is the LAST member and guard 9 pins the far end of the table. Exit 42 = szNull 0 + (sizeof - 200) 0 + tail-pad 0 + offLast/8 24 + offIntrospect/8 12 + offSize/8 2 + (g_bump - 3) 4; szNull (the zone's own size() of a non-allocation) is asserted ONLY by the sum, and g_bump is a mutable global, so nothing here folds to a literal. The macho-only targets are DELIBERATE: `malloc/malloc.json` is availableObjectFormats [macho] and zones are an Apple libmalloc concept with no glibc or UCRT counterpart, so the two Darwin arches ARE the whole honest surface (the macos-latest CI leg; the shipped_flock_statfs_sysctl_zone_macho shape). BOTH arches are targeted, not one, and that is load-bearing rather than thorough: `structs[0]` carries TWO variant arms (mach `boolean_t` makes `claimed_address` return `int` on arm64 and `unsigned int` on x86_64), the selector requires exactly one match, and a typo in the arm nobody builds is invisible — an assertion measured on one leg is a portability claim. Both arms were RUN before this manifest listed them: ✔MEASURED 2026-09-01 on the operator's Mac (macOS 26.6.2, arm64), the arm64 artifact exits 42 natively and the x86_64 artifact exits 42 under Rosetta, debug and release. RED-ON-DISABLE: restore the `__opaque_tail` form of malloc.json's structs[0] -> every z-><member> past `size` is a missing member and there is no binary (the descriptor shadows the real SDK header totally); move any single offset and guard 4..9 returns its own number; re-model `version` 8 bytes wide and guard 8 returns; delete the x86_64 variant arm and the arm64 build stays green while an x86_64 one stops compiling. The release arm re-runs every member call under the full optimizer, where a wrong member type would be folded rather than loaded.
